items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard Buster Moten, the brother of Benny Moten playing a piano accordion, and he would really swing on it.

ctx.x: When the two weeks with the Bean (as Hawk was also known) were finished, he asked me if I would like to stay longer, but Kirby had received an offer to play in a white club in Baltimore. I was lonesome for the Eastern part of the country, and Baltimore being only a few hours by train from New York City, I was happy to be going away from Los Angeles. So I refused Hawk's offer, and a few days later, we were on a train bringing us back East. Fir the first time and the last time in my life, I saw some parts of the…

The trip was five days coming to Baltimore, the same as it had been going to California, and when we arrived, Kirby had hired a local pianist and drummer for the club job. There was a white girl named Ginger in the floor show, and she was the first woman I ever heard play an accordion. I had heard Buster Moten, the brother of Benny Moten playing a piano accordion, and he would really swing on it. Ginger was not a jazz accordionist, but she played a nice commercial style. We often played black jack between sets,…
(***Ram had left the orchestra after the plantation dates)
